sections.content: How many people are "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants"?

20,725 people

were counted on the census as "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants make funeral arrangements for clients, prepare the deceased for burial or cremation, and supervise and assist the proceedings of funerals.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants", 15.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" included:

  • caretakers
  • shopkeepers and owners - retail and wholesale
  • typists and related keyboard occupations

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" there were more men than women (60% compared with 40%).

This means "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "caring personal service occupations".

Men made up 60% and women made up 40% of "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" included:

  • finance and investment analysts and advisers
  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors
  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "undertakers, mortuary and crematorium assistants", 12.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (64% compared with 36%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (84.3%) than self-employed (15.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
